sources.entry: Opik ⚠ - Evaluate, test, and ship LLM applications with a suite of observability tools to calibrate language model outputs across your dev and production lifecycle. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Docker/Python

summary.one_liner: Opik is an Apache-2.0 open-source platform for LLM and AI agent observability, tracing, evaluation, prompt management, and production monitoring that can be self-hosted.
summary.what_it_does: Opik logs LLM calls and multi-step agent activity as trace trees, via a Python SDK, a TypeScript SDK, OpenTelemetry, a REST API, or a long list of framework integrations. The @track decorator records any Python function, including nested calls. It supports datasets, experiments, and LLM-as-a-judge metrics such as hallucination detection, moderation, and RAG assessment, plus heuristic metrics and custom metrics. It includes a Prompt Playground, online evaluation rules and dashboards for production monitoring, and a PyTest integration for running evaluations in CI/CD. The README also mentions the Opik Agent Optimizer SDK and Opik Guardrails. The server can be run with Docker Compose via an opik.sh or opik.ps1 script, or on Kubernetes with a Helm chart, or used through Comet.com Cloud.
use_cases: trace LLM calls and AI agent steps
evaluate LLM application outputs with datasets and experiments
monitor production LLM traffic and token usage
run LLM evaluations in CI/CD with PyTest
self-host LLM observability inside own infrastructure
how_to_run: git clone the opik repository and cd opik
./opik.sh (Linux/Mac) or powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c ".\opik.ps1" (Windows) to start the local Docker Compose platform
Open localhost:5173 in a browser once containers are running
For scalable deployments, install the Helm chart as described in the Kubernetes guide
notable: Full platform including backend and web app is Apache-2.0 licensed and self-hostable without an enterprise license
Framework-agnostic with a large list of native integrations (OpenAI, LangChain, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, Google ADK, and many more)
Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, Codex and opencode can read traces and run evaluations via an MCP server (uvx opik mcp configure)
Any language with an OpenTelemetry SDK can send traces to Opik
caveats: Self-hosted setup requires Docker for the quick local install; Kubernetes/Helm is needed for larger deployments
The MCP badges and fallback commands target Opik Cloud, per the README
Guardrails are an optional add-on enabled with a --guardrails flag
keywords: monitor my ai agent in production
